Writing documents

A document is a Markdown file named name.mkp.md. Write Markdown first, and reach for a widget only where the reader should do something: change a value, step through, answer.

Decide in this order:

  1. Plain Markdown, when the reader only reads.
  2. A widget a pack gives, filled in with YAML.
  3. A copy of one, edited, when one does nearly everything you need.
  4. Your own, composed from the base set, when nothing comes close.

#Markdown

Headings, paragraphs, lists and task lists, tables, quotes and alerts (> [!TIP]), code, maths, footnotes and images all work as they do on GitHub. Each is a block of the base set, so it comes out as itself in every output.

Maths is TeX between dollars: $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$ gives , and a display formula goes between $$ lines:

A fence labelled with a language (sh, ts, yaml, markdown, text…) is always code, and a math fence is always a formula, whatever is inside.

#Widget blocks

A widget block is a fence named after the widget, with its inputs in YAML and a summary:, one sentence saying what the reader sees:

```counter
start: 3
summary: A counter that starts at 3.
```
  • Quote text in YAML when it could read as something else: on: no is the text "no", but on: false is a boolean, and '\theta' keeps its backslash where "\theta" would not.
  • A block may carry an id after its name, ````counter #score`, for a host to find it by.
  • A label Markdown already knows (a language, text, math) never names a widget: the fence stays Markdown.

#Shared state

Two widgets can read the same value. A state block declares it once, with the control that changes it, and each block reads it with {ref: name}:

```state
celsius = slider -20..40 step=1 = 18 "temperature in °C"
```

```thermometer
t: {ref: celsius}
scale: c
summary: The temperature in Celsius.
```

```thermometer
t: {ref: celsius}
scale: f
summary: The same temperature in Fahrenheit.
```

Moving the one slider moves both. See it in the examples.

#Containers

What goes inside a widget (Markdown, other widget blocks, more containers) is written between :::name and :::, never in YAML. The widget's other inputs go on the opening line:

:::tabs
:::tab "Idea"
Split the list, sort each half, merge.
:::
:::tab "Try it"
```question
prompt: How many passes for 8 items?
kind: number
value: 3
summary: Passes for eight items.
```
:::
:::

The content fills the widget's first slot; :::fill name … ::: fills another. Putting content in YAML instead is refused (mkp.slot-in-yaml), so the data and the content never mix.

#Widgets from a pack

A pack (name.mkpack, or a folder) is a library of widgets a host loads. Name it when you check or build, and list what it gives:

mkp index --pack lib                    # every widget, one a line
mkp show walk --pack lib                # one widget's inputs and an example
mkp show walk --pack lib --source --as my-walk   # its source, renamed, to paste and edit

A copy belongs to your document: nothing links it back, so a later change to the pack never reaches it.

#Front matter

A document may start with YAML front matter, as these pages do. MKP keeps it in the build for the host (a title, tags, a description) and draws none of it.

#Checking

Run mkp check until it is clean. Every error names its rule, its line and column, what was found, and the fix:

lesson.mkp.md:17:5 error mkp.input-type: xs[1] is a number; found "four"

--format json gives one error a line, for an editor or an agent to read.
